Poetic form: Shakespearean sonnet
Fourteen lines, conventionally in iambic pentameter: three quatrains followed by a couplet.
Rhyme arrangement: ABAB CDCD EFEF GG.

Poetic form: Petrarchan sonnet
Fourteen lines divided into an octave and a sestet. The octave commonly uses ABBAABBA; sestet rhymes vary. A turn in the argument often occurs between them.

Poetic form: Villanelle
Nineteen lines: five tercets, then a quatrain. The opening stanza's first and third lines recur as refrains, becoming the final two lines.
Pattern: A1 b A2 / a b A1 / a b A2 / a b A1 / a b A2 / a b A1 A2.

Poetic form: Sestina
Six stanzas of six lines recycle six end words, followed by a three-line envoi using all six.
End-word order: ABCDEF / FAEBDC / CFDABE / ECBFAD / DEACFB / BDFECA.

Poetic form: Terza rima
Three-line stanzas are linked: the middle rhyme of one becomes the outer rhyme of the next.
Pattern: ABA BCB CDC DED ...
